insights_auto
Reliance Industries fluctuated over the past month as mixed segment performance balanced broader market volatility. Primary drivers include retail expansion and steady telecom performance alongside weak refining margins. Market consensus suggests analysts project modest near-term growth pending clearer timelines for highly anticipated telecom and retail IPOs.
Reliance Industries fluctuated over the past month as mixed segment performance balanced broader market volatility. Primary drivers include retail expansion and steady telecom performance alongside weak refining margins. Market consensus suggests analysts project modest near-term growth pending clearer timelines for highly anticipated telecom and retail IPOs.
OutlookFrom TipRanks news sentiment reports
100.0% bullish
trending_upBullish view
  • Strong Telecom and Digital Momentum: Jio continues to show robust subscriber addition metrics and improved average revenue per user following tariff hikes, solidifying its dominant position in the digital ecosystem.
  • Anticipated Retail and Telecom IPOs: Investor sentiment remains heavily supported by value-unlocking prospects, as long-term market expectations focus on potential value separation through public listings of its retail and telecom arms.
trending_downBearish view
  • Weak Refining and Petrochemical Margins: The oil-to-chemicals segment faces intense margin compression as global refining margins soften, creating persistent earnings headwinds for the company's legacy business.
  • High Capital Expenditure Budgets: Massive ongoing investments in 5G expansion and new green energy initiatives continue to impact near-term free cash flow generation and elevate net debt concerns.

Profile
Reliance Industries Limited is an Indian multinational conglomerate headquartered in Mumbai. Its businesses include energy, petrochemicals, natural gas, retail, entertainment, telecommunications, mass media, and textiles. Reliance is the largest public company in India by market capitalisation and revenue, and the 88th largest company worldwide. It is India's largest private tax payer and largest exporter, accounting for 7% of India's total merchandise exports. The company has attracted controversy for reports of political corruption, cronyism, fraud, financial manipulation, and exploitation of its customers, Indian citizens, and natural resources. Fiscal Q1 2027 earnings call
slide_libraryPresentation Slides
Three-Year Retail EBITDA Doubling Plan
24m 2s
Management announced a bold strategic ambition to double absolute retail EBITDA over the next three years. Investors will appreciate this growth target, which shifts focus away from near-term margin compression caused by aggressive dark store investments toward long-term profitability and operational leverage driven by a rapidly scaling digital commerce business.
1 / 4
Ethane Cracking Cost Advantage
62m 1s
Reliance highlighted a major competitive advantage in its petrochemical business, where ethane and ROGC comprise 70% of ethylene feedstock. As global naphtha costs soared past $1,000 per ton, softer U.S. ethane prices widened cracking deltas significantly, protecting margins and pleasing investors concerned with feedstock price volatility.
2 / 4
New Energy Gigafactory Timeline Secured
74m 42s
Management moved from strategy to tangible execution by confirming that its 20 GW solar PV and 40 GWh battery gigafactories in Jamnagar will commission this year. This milestone satisfies long-standing investor demand for clear execution timelines on multi-billion dollar capital allocations to the green energy segment.
3 / 4
Meta Partnership for Megawatt Data Center
95m 5s
Reliance announced a massive partnership with Meta to build an end-to-end 168 MW data center in Jamnagar funded entirely via its own balance sheet. Investors will celebrate this strategic expansion into high-growth AI and compute infrastructure, alongside the validation of Reliance's unique ability to deliver fully integrated network and power services.
4 / 4

Call transcript
summarize_auto
Reliance Industries reported consolidated top-line growth of 25% year-over-year, driven by elevated oil prices, alongside 12% revenue growth in both Jio and Retail segments. Overall EBITDA rose 10% to over INR 54,000 crores, and net profit grew 6% to nearly INR 23,200 crores, when adjusting for prior-year one-offs.
expand_more
summarize_auto
Highlights
  • Reliance Industries reported consolidated top-line growth of 25% year-over-year, driven by elevated oil prices, alongside 12% revenue growth in both Jio and Retail segments. Overall EBITDA rose 10% to over INR 54,000 crores, and net profit grew 6% to nearly INR 23,200 crores, when adjusting for prior-year one-offs.
Srikanth Venkatachari, CFO, Reliance Industries
This has been an extraordinary quarter. Extraordinary when you look at it from point of view of macro volatility. Extraordinary if you see it from point of view of energy market shock. Extraordinary when you think of it in the context of what kind of supply chain dislocation that happened. In that context is where when you look at the overall performance, I do want to say that it's been an extraordinary performance too. The kind of agility we have shown has been incredible, and I'll tell you why it is. Starting with the numbers, top line up 25%, primarily because of oil prices. It is also a fact that Jio top line was also up 12%, even retail was up close to 12%. It's not just about O2C.

When you look at that, our overall EBITDA is more than INR 54,000 crores, we are up 10%. Net profit at almost close to INR 23,200, again up 6%. When you see the numbers, strong performance by O2C up 17%, JPL 15%. Those were the standout performance, and we will also talk about the other businesses. Again, consumer businesses is now again back to, it's about 50% of the overall mix.

I just wanted to say that those numbers are there, but I think those numbers are on a flat crude basis, and it doesn't provide for the fact that you had to pay higher differentials to acquire the crude. Broadly, performance is on the back of higher spreads. Deltas, even chemical deltas, three to four years high. insights_autoReliance Beats on All Fronts:Reliance Industries reported a reported adjusted EPS of 15.48, beating the estimated 14.974, and generated reported revenue of ₹3,160,180 million, outperforming the estimated ₹3,055,513 million.
insights_autoEnergy Drives Operational Excellence:The Oil-to-Chemicals segment led earnings with an EBITDA growth of 17.2% year-over-year, supported by strong petrochemical margins and high middle distillate cracks.
insights_autoOptimism Rooted in Jio IPO:Management expressed strong forward optimism for the fiscal year, highlighting plans to unlock significant value through the upcoming Jio IPO and the phased commissioning of new energy projects.
insights_autoDigital Services Show Healthy Expansion:Jio Platforms grew its digital services EBITDA by 16.1% year-over-year, supported by subscriber upgrades and an average revenue per user (ARPU) climbing to nearly ₹216.
insights_autoInfrastructure Outlays Cool Retail Margins:Reliance Retail experienced a 14% year-over-year decline in net profit down to ₹2,805 crore, reflecting heavy investments in expanding its digital commerce infrastructure.
